name: inprocess-cva6-axi4-timer-f5
notes: CVA6 packed AXI4 CPU through the existing axi4_processor_memory_adapter; the target is the PULP APB3 timer at 0x40001000. Program slot is 0x12000, inside the execute-but-uncached 0x10000..0x20000 window.

The interrupt entry is the built model's irq_i input (2 bits). This host drives bit 0 only: the profile declares irq_i[0] as the machine-external entry (mip_d[riscv::IRQ_M_EXT] = irq_i[0], core/csr_regfile.sv:2073) and holds irq_i[1] (supervisor external, IRQ_S_EXT) at constant 0 (component profile port_actions, bits [1]). Bit 0 is taken in M-mode because the firmware bootstrap installs mtvec and enables mstatus.MIE + mie.MEIE; bit 1 is never claimed as a vector.

The take witness is rvfi_intr together with the commit lane's cause: an interrupt retirement with cause 0x800000000000000b (machine external) and the privilege it entered. The case line prints irq_takes from that witness; the run log prints the trap record and an irq_take line carrying the cause and mode.

F5 is the timer's declared pulse path: trigger writes [[4,0],[8,0],[0,0xffffffff]], status TIMER0_COUNT at offset 0, no clear. The ISR reads the count (not a cause: the profile declares no cause bits).
description: One CVA6 packed AXI4 CPU reaches the PULP APB3 timer. The CPU's declared interrupt entry is the two-bit irq_i port: bit 0 is the machine-external line this host drives from the timer's real irq_o[0], and bit 1 is the supervisor-external line the profile itself holds inactive (port_actions irq_i constant 0, bits [1]); the take is observed on the retirement face (an interrupt retire with cause 0x800000000000000b in M-mode), never inferred from an ISR store.
